top.title: Deonte Banks Tops Giants Contract List With 14 Pass Breakups
top.description: New York Giants cornerback Deonte Banks (2) runs with the ball after an interception during a week 11 NFL football game between New York Giants and Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The New York Giants face a tight window to lock up cornerback Deonte Banks before his contract expires. On Tuesday, Jordan Raanan of ESPN identified Banks as the leading candidate for a contract extension. With 14 pass breakups, the 2023 first-round pick shares the league lead. He enters the final season of his rookie deal, which totals $13.59 million over four years. The team declined his fifth-year option back in May, a move that could cost them dearly now. Banks has turned his career around after being written off by the previous coaching staff. He took the starting job from Paulson Adebo in training camp before the 2026 season. Adebo signed a massive $54 million deal last year, only to lose his spot to a player he was meant to mentor. Alex Wilson from Empire State Media posted on his official X account, “If the depth chart is legit, my god … Paulson Adebo, how did you lose a starting job to Deonte Banks!!!” Setting the Market Price The Denver Broncos recently set a new bar for cornerbacks in their draft class. They signed Riley Moss to a four-year, $67 million extension. That breaks down to $16.75 million per year. The Athletic’s Dan Duggan noted, “Greg Newsome got $15.25M. Data points to keep in mind for Deonte Banks’ negotiations.” Newsome, another Giants cornerback, signed a three-year, $46 million deal earlier this month. The Giants should aim for that range to keep their secondary intact without overpaying. The Athletic’s Dan Duggan wrote, “Looks wise for Greg Newsome to lock in his extension eight games into the season.” He added that missing time with a “serious” high-ankle sprain could hurt a player’s market value. Banks has no such injury concerns and is playing at an elite level right now. Waiting until he hits the open market could push his value well past $20 million per year. The Quarterback Question Looms While the defense shines, the quarterback room remains a complex issue. J.J. McCarthy has started 3-1 for the Giants after replacing Jameis Winston. However, the team still holds onto 2025 first-round pick Jaxson Dart. Although a knee injury cost McCarthy his entire rookie year, he holds a 9-5 record as a starter across his first two seasons. ESPN’s Bill Barnwell asked, “What happens when Jaxson Dart is healthy?” The Giants traded only a fifth-round pick to get McCarthy, leaving them with leverage if they choose to move him. In 2027, Brent Sobleski of Bleacher Report projected McCarthy to be the ideal match for the Pittsburgh Steelers. He noted, “For now, Dart remains the presumed long-term preference in New York.” The Steelers need a new quarterback soon as Aaron Rodgers retires after this season. top.title: A year after KKR release, Mustafizur Rahman missing from IPL auction list as 11 Bangladesh players register
top.description: Mustafizur Rahman is not among the 11 Bangladesh players who have registered for the IPL 2027 auction, which will be held in Goa on December 16. The left-arm pacer was released by Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) on the BCCI's instructions last year, a decision that eventually led to Bangladesh withdrawing from the T20 World Cup in India. BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia did not specify the reason behind Mustafizur's release at the time, saying only that it was due to "recent developments". The 11 Bangladesh players who have entered the auction are Hasan Mahmud, Parvez Hossain Emon, Ripon Mondol, Rishad Hossain, Saif Hassan, Shak Mahedi Hasan, Shamim Hossain, Shoriful Islam, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Towhid Hridoy and Md Rubel. Stokes enters IPL auction Former England captain Ben Stokes and Australian batter Cameron Bancroft are among the prominent overseas players who have registered for the auction. Stokes, who retired from international cricket earlier this year, has set his base price at Rs 2 crore. The 35-year-old last played in the IPL in 2023, when he featured in two matches for Chennai Super Kings. He has also represented Rajasthan Royals and the now-defunct Rising Pune Supergiant. Bancroft, who has recently sought to clarify his role in the 2018 ball-tampering scandal and responded to claims made by Pat Cummins, has registered at a base price of Rs 75 lakh. The 34-year-old has never played in the IPL but regularly features in the Big Bash League. Australian fast bowler Scott Boland has also registered, although he is not expected to be available for most of the tournament. Japan's Benjamin Ito Davis is among the players from associate nations who could go under the hammer. He has set his base price at Rs 30 lakh. A total of 1,220 players have registered for the auction, including 939 Indians and 281 overseas players. The 10 teams have a maximum of 66 slots to fill, including 25 for overseas players. The list is expected to be cut down significantly before the auction. The registration list includes 184 capped players, 994 uncapped players and 42 players from associate nations. The 10 franchises have retained a total of 184 players. 136154481 Fourteen capped Indian players have also registered for the auction. They are Akash Deep, Avesh Khan, Deepak Chahar, Deepak Hooda, Jaydev Unadkat, Karun Nair, Kuldeep Sen, Mayank Agarwal, Umesh Yadav, Umran Malik, Saransh Jain, Shivam Mavi, Tushar Deshpande and Rahul Tripathi.

top.title: Ben Johnson Keeps D’Andre Swift In Bears Run Game Despite Fumble
top.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images D’Andre Swift will not lose his spot as the lead back for the Chicago Bears after a costly mistake against the New Orleans Saints. Head coach Ben Johnson made his stance clear on Tuesday. The coach rejected the idea that Swift must work to earn back any trust. He said the running back simply needs to secure the football to keep the offense moving forward. Swift lost his third fumble of the season during the fourth quarter. New Orleans recovered the ball at their own 46-yard line. The 27-year-old runner did not return to the game after that turnover. It marks the second time this year Swift was pulled from a lineup for a fumble. Despite these errors, the coach insists the team will keep relying on its rushing attack. The Trust Factor When asked if Swift needs to regain confidence from the coaching staff, Johnson shut down the notion immediately. “No, he just needs to hold on to the ball and we’ll be fine,” Johnson said, according to ESPN . This comment came after the Bears secured a 21-13 win over the Saints on Sunday. The victory improved the team’s record, and the coaching staff continues to focus on ball security. Swift has fumbled three times through the first ten games. This is the most he has lost since the 2023 season. Michal Dwojak noted that Swift still holds the head coach’s trust according to RotoBaller. In that game, the veteran back recorded his first touchdown catch of the year. He led the backfield with 15 touches, including two catches for eight yards and a score. Running Game Efficiency The Bears offense relies heavily on moving the chains on the ground. The team ranks third in the league with 142.4 rushing yards per game. However, Johnson was not happy with the efficiency numbers in the recent win. The team rushed for 146 yards against New Orleans, their third-highest total of the year. Yet the average yards per carry fell short of the goal. “We weren’t as consistent running the ball as we had wanted to be coming off the bye, that was a point of emphasis for us,” Johnson said postgame. Swift ran 13 times for 51 yards, averaging 3.9 yards per carry. Johnson pointed out that the runners were under four yards a carry. “When I looked at our runners, they were under four yards a carry. That efficiency stat that we talked about, we weren’t hitting that,” Johnson said. Upcoming Matchup Other backs saw action in the game as well. In his first game back after toe and thumb injuries, Kyle Monangai rushed eight times for 18 yards. Monangai played 23 offensive snaps compared to Swift’s 28. Salvon Ahmed added six carries to the mix. The coaching staff will look to balance the workload while fixing the ball security issues before the next game. “We’re going to continue to stress that running game,” Johnson said Tuesday. The Bears must prepare for a tough road test against a division rival. The team will face the Detroit Lions on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 1 p.m. ET at Ford Field.

top.title: FC Barcelona Vs Sabah Line Up: Solutions And Rotations Without Lamine
top.description: FC Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick will make several rotations for Wednesday's Champions League trip to Baku. Getty Images FC Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick will make several rotations to his first XI in Wednesday’s Champions League league phase encounter against Sabah. We already knew that Lamine Yamal wouldn’t travel to Baku, after the club released a statement explaining that the youngster is suffering from ankle discomfort. At a prematch press conference on Tuesday, Flick said that a decision was made for the Ballon d’Or candidate to stay behind in Catalunya with an eye on the team’s big picture ambitions. “We’ve played without Lamine in the past; he’s very important to us. Considering our long-term goal, we decided he wouldn’t travel as a precaution,” the manager explained. It was also hinted that Pau Cubarsi might be rested too. “He can play if he’s ready,” Flick explained. “I’ve usually tried to manage him to be as fit as possible. If we can manage the team without him tomorrow, we will. If we can rest him, we will.” This will become a reality, in that Eric Garcia and a Gerard Martin who was monstrous last time out against Villarreal will man central defence while protecting Joan Garcia’s goal. On the flanks, Joao Cancelo starts to the left while Jules Kounde should get the nod over on the right channel despite his lateness to training. The midfield will see Frenkie de Jong rewarded for a strong defensive showing in the 3-2 comeback win against Villarreal and Gavi being handed a rare start. Fermin Lopez is the CAM ahead of the midfield duo as Dani Olmo continues to recover. And on the right wing, in Lamine’s place, it’s Karim Adeyemi. That means that there’s no place for Gabriel Jesus up front, at least not from the offset. Instead, it’s Raphinha as the central number 9 while Anthony Gordon looks to score against a team he netted four past before half time last term while still donning a Newcastle United shirt. What FC Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick said "It’s [Sabah] a team that likes to play good football. That is its pattern. The most important thing in this match is attitude. It’s the Champions League and we respect every opponent.” FC Barcelona Vs Sabah Expected XI: Garcia; Cancelo, Gerard, Eric, Kounde; De Jong, Gavi, Gordon, Fermin, Adeyemi; Raphinha This article was originally published on Forbes.com

top.title: Rinderknech denies refusing doping test
top.description: Arthur Rinderknech is yet to win an ATP title and reached a highest world ranking of 24th in May [Getty Images] French tennis player Arthur Rinderknech says he expects to be exonerated over allegations he refused a doping test. L'Equipe reported on Wednesday that the current world number 57 is under investigation by the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA). It relates to a "surprise" test in June, with French newspaper L'Equipe claiming there was a "possible misunderstanding with the sample collector". Former Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova is currently serving a four-year ban for refusing to take an out-of-competition doping test in December 2025, and has appealed against the decision. Rinderknech issued a statement on Instagram in response to L'Equipe's report, saying: "I have already advised the ITIA that I deny the allegation and I have already requested that the matter be heard and determined by an independent tribunal, as is my right." The 31-year-old, who beat current world number one Alexander Zverev in the first round at Wimbledon last year, believes he will then be "exonerated of the test refusal allegation". "I have never taken any banned substance and I am proud of my accomplishments in professional tennis, all of which have been achieved through hard work and with integrity always," he added. top.title: Jude Bellingham explains why he’s no match for Zinedine Zidane after shining for Real Madrid
top.description: Jude Bellingham has played down comparisons to Real Madrid legend Zinedine Zidane after inspiring victory in the Champions League with a sensational goal against PSV. The England international juggled the ball in the air before swiping a volley into the back of the net, leaving fans and teammates in awe, including Bernardo Silva: “It was one of those moments when you just go, ‘Wow!’” The win maintains Madrid’s perfect Champions League record, elevating them to serious contenders to dethrone two-time defending champions Paris Saint-Germain, while rising up The Independent’s power rankings . And after Mourinho described Bellingham as “without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world,” comparisons continue with one of Madrid’s all-time greatest players: Zidane. But Bellingham was quick to distance himself from the conversation, instead placing the France manager in an entirely different category. "I was a bit surprised, honestly. I knew that I could control the ball well and get it into my grasp. But normally from there, I'm looking to see who's on as an option to play through,” Bellingham said when asked about his goal before addressing talk that he is on the same level as Zidane. "It popped up nicely and I thought I'm just going to hit it. So yeah, it was a nice goal and important for the team, being the second goal, and gave us control. Bellingham scored a stunning volley in the second half (Getty) "I think Zidane is much better than me. He's much more elegant and he's my idol.” Mourinho was left stunned by his player’s latest impact, pinpointing just what makes him so good. "He is an amazing player that has everything," the Portuguese manager said. "He has physicality, he understands the game, he has absolutely everything. Today, he has changed how the game was evolving." “Obviously Jude is a different type of player and he gave us what we didn't have in the first half,” Mourinho said. “He changed the game, scored an incredible goal.”

top.title: As Farmageddon's streak ends, Kansas State and Iowa State hope it's not for long
top.description: MANHATTAN — When Skylar Thompson first arrived at Kansas State , he knew about the rivalry against Kansas, but when he sat at a team dinner and heard the seniors talk about the importance of beating Iowa State , he learned there was a second rivalry that was almost as important . Winning that game suddenly didn't matter as much for personal pride . Instead, it became about winning for the fanbase, the seniors and the university. Thompson was behind center as a redshirt freshman in 2017 when the Wildcats were down by five against the Cyclones with eight seconds left from the one-yard line. Thompson looked to his left, and no one was open as he scrambled that way. With a defender in his face, he changed direction to the other side of the field. He ran, seemingly forever, until he found Isaiah Zuber in the back of the endzone as time expired . Wildcats win. "That was probably one of my most fond memories at K-State," Thompson said. Nicknamed "Farmageddon" for the agricultural roots of being two land-grant universities, Kansas State and Iowa State have played the longest uninterrupted continuous series in college football, having played each season since 1917. The 110th-straight game between the two will be played on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 1 p.m. CT at Jack Trice Stadium in Ames, Iowa. Saturday will also mark the end of the uninterrupted series, as the two are not scheduled to play next season. "We definitely wanted to play it," K-State athletic director Gene Taylor said. "But we knew that everybody was gonna get to play a second rival. We kind of had to take our lumps and agree to the way the scheduling matrix turned out." When the Big 12 added Arizona, Arizona State , Colorado and Utah to expand the league to 16 teams, the reconfigured scheduling matrix chose four "protected" rivalries that wouldn't go away, and Kansas State-Kansas was one of them. That put Farmageddon on the chopping block. When the matrix was released ahead of the 2024 season, it was known the Wildcats' annual game against the Cyclones would end in 2027. A new matrix will need to be developed ahead of the 2028 season, which could see the return of the game sooner rather than later. That's something Taylor expects to happen. With all of the changes in the sport, especially with the 24-team College Football Playoff that will begin in 2027, scheduling will be at the forefront. "I think it may not be as long of a hiatus as we think it was; in essence, there was gonna be a period of 2-3 years where we weren't going to play," Taylor said. "We may have to rethink the entire scheduling model here coming up. I think our fanbase wanted to keep it; there's no question. I think there's a lot of reasons to keep it in the future." Farmageddon predated the Big 8, let alone the Big 12, beginning in 1917 when K-State and Iowa State were both members of a previous iteration of the Missouri Valley Conference. top.title: Bills vs Chiefs prediction, key matchups in Thanksgiving showdown
top.description: ORCHARD PARK - The No. 1 seed in the AFC will not be decided Thursday night when the Buffalo Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs in a Thanksgiving showdown befitting one of the biggest national TV windows there is on the NFL schedule. But for the 9-1 Bills in particular, already starting with a one-game advantage on the 8-2 Chiefs, if they can find their way to a victory, they are going to be set up in prime position to grab that elusive spot which they have not enjoyed since the 1993 season. A win would provide Buffalo an important head-to-head tiebreaker advantage meaning the Bills would technically be 2.5 games ahead of Kansas City with six to play. With the Jaguars and Bengals suffering rather inexplicable Week 11 losses, they each have three losses, so Buffalo’s main competition would be the Broncos who go into their Black Friday game in Pittsburgh with an 8-2 record. Flip it around, though, and a Chiefs victory pulls them even with the Bills and gives Kansas City the head-to-head tiebreaker, immediately moving the Chiefs ahead of Buffalo. Denver could also move past the Bills with a win while the Jaguars and Bengals would be just one loss behind. In its promotional material for the game, NBC referred to Bills vs. Chiefs as the “Rivalry of the Decade” and ranked it as the best non-division rivalry since the NFL’s playoff format was altered in 1990, putting it in the same class as Colts-Patriots in the 2000s, and 49ers-Cowboys in the 1990s. They have split 10 games counting the postseason, there have been six one-score games in the bunch, and the teams rank 1-2 in victories in the 2020s, the Bills at 82 and the Chiefs 80. The Hoosiers (9-2, 6-2 Big Ten) dropped six spots to No. 14 , below all the other Big Ten contenders and outside the cut line for the 12-team field. Hunter Yurachek the Arkansas athletic director who serves as the CFP selection committee chair, pointed to several key factors to explain IU's drop on Tuesday night. top.title: Hillsdale Academy soccer athletes earn six all-state honors
top.description: HILLSDALE — Hillsdale Academy boys soccer capped off another successful fall season with six players earning Division 4 all-state recognition from the Michigan High School Soccer Coaches Association. More: Youngman family runs together, bonds together The Colts finished the 2026 season with a 15-4-2 overall record, capturing their seventh consecutive district championship and reaching the Division 4 regional championship game for the first time since 2020. Junior midfielder Danny Aburto-Rodriguez led the Colts’ postseason honors with a second-team all-state selection. Fellow junior midfielder and cousin Rene Rodriguez earned third-team all-state recognition. Four additional Colts received honorable mention honors, including senior forward Justin Busby, senior defender Hudson Mackie, senior midfielder Andrew Richards and junior goalkeeper Robert Whalen. The six honorees helped lead Hillsdale Academy through another memorable postseason run under longtime head coach Neal Brady. Season review The Colts captured their seventh consecutive district title with a dramatic 3-2 double-overtime victory over Jackson Christian on Oct. 24. Busby delivered the championship-winning goal off an assist from Rene Rodriguez less than a minute into the second overtime period. The victory also marked Brady’s 300th-career coaching win. Hillsdale Academy followed its district championship with an 8-0 shutout of Ypsilanti Arbor Prep in the regional semifinals. Busby scored five goals in the victory, helping the Colts advance to their first regional final appearance in six years. The Colts’ season ended with a 2-0 loss to familiar postseason rival Grosse Pointe Woods University Liggett in the Division 4, Region 15 championship on Oct. 29. Busby, who helped lead the Colts’ offense throughout their championship run, reflected on the relationships he built with his teammates. “We, at the end of the season, became more than just teammates. We became brothers,” Busby said. “This is probably the closest our team’s been since I’ve been here.” The Colts now turn their attention toward 2027, returning both Rodriguez midfielders and Whalen in goal while saying goodbye to a senior class that helped extend one of the program’s most successful stretches. top.title: Missouri faces Oklahoma offense that's found new life in November
top.description: Film study on Oklahoma in the Mizzou football defensive meeting room isn’t reaching much outside of the month of November. The Tigers (7-4, 4-4 SEC) will take on Oklahoma (7-5, 5-3) on Saturday on Faurot Field to round out the regular season. Win, and the Tigers will finish in the top half of the SEC. They’ll almost certainly finish the regular season ranked in the top 25 in all the major polls. Eli Drinkwitz has contract implications on the line , too, as an eighth regular season automatically extends his deal by one year. The matchup against the Sooners is going to bring the typical challenges on defense and special teams. Brent Venables’ defense is, as is usually the case, among the better statistical units in the conference. Oklahoma has the SEC’s leading punt returner, Isaiah Sategna III, who has returned two punts for touchdowns. But a new challenge has emerged. The once-woebegone OU offense has found a groove late in the season. Oklahoma made a change at offensive coordinator on Nov. 2, firing Ben Arbuckle and moving Jason Witten into an interim play-calling role. Since then, the Sooners have won three straight games, guaranteeing they’ll finish SEC play with a winning record, beating Florida, Ole Miss , and Texas A&M in succession. The difference? “I think they've committed to the run game,” MU head coach Eli Drinkwitz said. “They're committed to an identity of what they're trying to do in the pass game, and then they're utilizing Mateer’s legs as an extra weapon, and so I think anytime you have those three things coming together — identity in the run game, known pass game, you know, using that quarterback as that primary runner — that's very difficult on defense. Very difficult to figure out how you're going to stop the run.” That assessment checks out. Before the OC change, Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer was averaging nine carries per game for 32 rushing yards per game. Over the Sooners’ unbeaten last three matchups, he’s taken an average of 13.3 carries for 71.3 yards on the ground per game. “With a running quarterback, they have plus-one runs, and then he can also throw the ball pretty well,” MU linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez said. “So, you’ve got to be able to defend his legs and his arms. So, it's just kind of the battle you have to go through when you face a dual-threat quarterback.” Getting Mateer more involved on the ground has seemingly opened up the rest of the OU offense. The Sooners were struggling earlier in the season. In their first four games against Power-conference teams, they only managed 13 points once. top.title: Championship weekend has arrived, time for some football state finals picks
top.description: For the first time in a long time, northern Michigan is left out of the Thanksgiving weekend party at Ford Field. The MHSAA football state championships will take place for all eight 11-player divisions this weekend, but you won’t find a representative out of northern Michigan, or even the Upper Peninsula, for the first time in a while. Whether it’s been Kingsley or Traverse City St. Francis, Menominee or Negaunee, it feels like we’ve had someone to represent for a while. We’ve even had Cadillac, Traverse City Central and Glen Lake fighting for recent titles. The closest we get in 2026 is Beal City, though anyone that considers them northern Michigan has a Detroit area code in front of their phone number. But, even without a team in the final dance, there are plenty of great games to look forward to and some of the best players in the state in action ahead. Games will be played on Friday and Saturday, Nov. 27-28 at Ford Field in Detroit, with game times listed below. Four games will take place each day. While we don’t have any local teams playing, there are plenty of familiar teams to pick from below. DIVISION 1 Detroit Catholic Central (12-1) vs. Romeo (13-0) 7 p.m., Saturday What a story Romeo has been this season, capped by a 30-29 win over powerhouse Detroit Cass Tech a week ago, pulling ahead on a 2-point conversion inside two minutes. Now, they get another state powerhouse and the defending Division 1 state champs. There’s so much firepower on this Catholic Central team, from five-star Texas Tech commit Gideon Gash and running back Ryan Jaafar, to an experienced QB in Duke Banta. Romeo is a tough team, but it feels like the great story ends here. Catholic Central 38, Romeo 20 DIVISION 2 Orchard Lake St. Mary’s (10-3) vs. Muskegon Mona Shores (12-1) 7 p.m., Friday St. Mary’s has won two straight titles, while Mona Shores pulled in two straight back in 2019-20. So, both programs aren’t new to Ford Field by any means. The difference here feels like the experience and talent of St. Mary QB Jabin Gonzalez, who has so much talent to work with, led by North Carolina commit Chad Willis. When did the Ohio State-Michigan rivalry begin? Some historians trace the rivalry to the " Toledo War ," a land dispute between Ohio and Michigan when Michigan was applying for statehood in the 19th century. top.title: WSL makes agreement with clubs to avoid gambling sponsors
top.description: WSL Football, the organisation responsible for operating the top two tiers of women’s football in the UK, has reached an agreement in principle for its clubs not to make sponsorship deals with betting companies. Instead, the organisation has agreed to pursue sponsorship deals with brands from different industries, reports The Athletic . The outlet states that six additional sponsorship opportunities were made available ahead of the 2024/25 season, and these were filled by Apple, Airbnb, British Gas, Mercedes, Tesco and WTW. While the agreement applies to WSL Football’s own commercial partnerships, it does not stop individual WSL or WSL2 clubs from signing sponsorship deals with gambling companies. Rather, it sets a different direction for WSL Football’s league-level partnerships, giving the leagues the chance to shape their own commercial future. The organisation wants to continue aiding the growth of the women’s domestic game, while combating issues such as player welfare, gambling-related online abuse and fluctuating attendances. The changes also come at a time when English football is starting to take a wider look at gambling and related sponsorships. At the start of this season, the Premier League’s voluntary ban on betting sponsors appearing on the front of match-day shirts came into effect, while the Premier League, EFL, FA and WSL also introduced a Code of Conduct for gambling-related sponsorship agreements in 2024. Nevertheless, betting companies still feature prominently among sponsors at clubs throughout the top divisions in the men’s game, with Betway signing a deal with Manchester United and clubs such as Leeds and Nottingham Forest also agreeing new deals over the summer.

top.description: The regular season comes to an end in Galaxy Stadium for the Texas Tech football team , with TCU coming to town for a Thanksgiving showdown under the lights. There's a lot going on here, but we'll begin with TCU, which will have a new coach running things and a new quarterback running the show. Well, not entirely new. Adam Schobel took the reins against Utah after starter Jaden Craig missed the game due to injury. TCU has already ruled Craig out for this week's game, so Schobel will take snaps and try to lead the upset over Texas Tech. The 6-foot-5 sophomore had one pass attempt this season before going 15-of-31 for 106 yards and throwing two interceptions against the Utes. But this game is less about matchups and more about what's on the line. What's at stake for Texas Tech football Things are pretty simple for the Red Raiders this week. Beat the Horned Frogs and they're heading back to AT&T Stadium on Dec. 4 for the Big 12 Conference championship game against Utah, which has already clinched a spot in the title encounter. A loss to TCU does two things. First, it makes Texas Tech wait another two days to figure out if it's heading to Arlington, needing BYU to lose to Cincinnati. Second, no win over TCU and no BYU loss means Tech can pretty much kiss its College Football Playoff chances goodbye. Speaking of the CFP, this could be an important factor in Tech's inclusion this year. Texas Tech currently has the one-loss appeal that could get them into the field as an at-large bid, likely on the road to start the bracket. Losing the game would wipe that possibility out entirely. Something to consider is that Texas Tech just getting to the Big 12 title game probably wouldn't keep them safe in the CFP field regardless of the outcome in Arlington. He spoke in an interview with Channels Television on Tuesday evening in Jalingo, Taraba State, after an Obi-Kwankwaso town hall meeting. Addressing concerns over the presence of weapons at political gatherings, Obi said the public had misunderstood the ‘rig and die’ calls against electoral malpractice as opposition to political campaigns. This is as he defended supporters of his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, over allegations that they carry sticks to political campaigns, saying the items have not been used to “harm anyone”. Obi insisted that he had not witnessed anyone being attacked with the stick-wielding Kwankwasiyya movement during political gatherings. “They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die.’ What we, people said is that they don’t want rigging this time. nigeria.description: Ufuoma Paula Onephrojire on the importance of childhood financial literacy, the inspiration behind her book, Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure , and her mission to raise a financially conscious generation. In a world where children are increasingly exposed to financial pressures, consumerism and unrealistic portrayals of wealth, teaching them how to manage money has become more important than ever. Yet, financial education remains largely absent from many children’s formative learning experiences. Following the launch of her children’s book, Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure , economist, financial literacy advocate and author, Ufuoma Paula Onephrojire, speaks about the personal experiences that inspired the book, why financial education must begin in childhood and her vision of making financial literacy accessible to children across Nigeria and Africa. Why should financial education begin in childhood? Interviewer: Financial literacy is increasingly becoming an important conversation among adults. Why are you making a case for introducing it to children? Ufuoma Paula: I believe we have waited too long to introduce children to conversations about money. We spend years teaching them how to read, write, calculate and prepare for examinations, but how much attention do we give to preparing them to make sound financial decisions? A child can graduate with excellent grades and still have no idea how to budget, save towards a goal, distinguish between needs and wants or manage money responsibly. Financial literacy is not something people suddenly need when they get their first salary. It is a life skill that is best developed early. Children already interact with money. They receive pocket money, make spending choices, compare what they own with what their friends have and develop attitudes towards money from what they observe at home and in society. Whether we deliberately teach them or not, they are learning something about money every day. The question is whether what they are learning is preparing them for responsible financial decisions. The lessons children learn about money today can influence the financial habits, values and decisions they carry into adulthood. Those decisions will affect not only their personal wellbeing, but also their families, businesses and communities. When we raise financially informed individuals, we are contributing to a society where people are better equipped to make responsible choices, recognise opportunities and manage resources wisely. We should teach children not just how to make money someday, but how to manage resources, recognise opportunities, create value and understand that money is a tool, not a master. nigeria.title: AGN mourns Pete Edochie, describes him as ‘father figure’
nigeria.description: By Benjamin Njoku The National President of the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN), Alhaji Abubakar Yakubu, has mourned veteran actor Pete Edochie, describing him as a father figure in the Nigerian entertainment industry whose legacy would endure for generations. Edochie, 79, reportedly died in the early hours of Wednesday following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. His son, Leo Pete Edochie, announced his death in an Instagram post, describing him as “our beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman.” In his tribute, Yakubu described the late actor as an all-rounder whose contributions extended beyond Nollywood to the broadcasting industry. “Pete Edochie was a man of the people, a detribalised Nigerian who spoke different languages. He lived a noble life, a dedicated Christian and a disciplinarian,” he said. He added that the actor’s death came at a time when the industry still needed his experience and contributions. “He died when the industry needed him most. But as a thorough-bred actor, he left when the ovation was loudest,” Yakubu said. Born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State, Edochie, fondly called Ebube Dike, hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, Anambra State. He began his career in broadcasting in 1967 with the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation, where he rose to become Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. He gained national prominence in the 1980s through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s literary classic, Things Fall Apart. The role earned him widespread recognition and helped launch a celebrated career in Nigerian cinema. Known for his deep voice, commanding delivery and rich use of proverbs, Edochie became synonymous with portrayals of kings, community leaders and family patriarchs. His notable film credits include Igodo, Rituals and Lionheart (2018), directed by Genevieve Nnaji. In recognition of his contributions to the entertainment industry, he was honoured with the Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003, the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards Industry Merit Award and several lifetime achievement honours. There was a time when Williams Alamu would rather not sit an examination than risk getting a grade he wasn’t happy with. A B or a C in his Cambridge A-levels felt like a possibility he wasn’t ready to entertain, so he didn’t write the exams. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. There were 5:30am wake-ups, difficult Statistics courses, friends who became unofficial tutors, a ChatGPT Pro subscription in 300 level, job offers he turned down and one Demography exam that kept him awake for 36 hours. University, as it turns out, came with quite a few plot twists. In this interview with BellaNaija, Williams takes us through the habits, people and decisions that shaped his academic journey. He also tells us whether he got that coveted top spot, what he learnt from the opportunities he put on hold, and what he would tell another student hoping to graduate with First-Class Honours. If that’s a goal you’re working towards, you may want to take notes. Literally or otherwise. Williams Alamu celebrates graduating with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. At what point did you realise you were chasing a record-breaking grade? Was it a goal from Day 1, or did it evolve? It was a goal from day one, actually. When I gained admission into the University of Ibadan, I already had my mind set on graduating as the Best Graduating Student in my faculty. I knew becoming the overall Best Graduating Student in the university would require an extraordinary amount of work, but I felt being the best in my faculty was something I wanted to work towards. And, of course, that would also mean graduating as the best student in my department. The motivation behind that goal goes back to shortly after secondary school, when my parents enrolled me in a Cambridge A-level programme. I went into it hoping to achieve three A-stars, but Chemistry was a major struggle. As the examinations approached, I became increasingly worried about my performance. I think I was more afraid of not meeting my own expectations than I was of the examination itself. entertainment.description: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. One where advice comes before the transaction, where due diligence is not treated as an inconvenience, and where people are encouraged to ask questions, understand their options and make informed decisions,” she said at the launch. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. The company is also building on experience gained before its official launch, having supported more than 25 clients with property opportunities across different markets. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. Fayemi’s position raises a familiar question: people consult doctors for medical concerns and lawyers for legal matters, so why do some investors leave significant property decisions in the hands of relatives simply because they are available or familiar with the location? While trust and family relationships matter, they do not automatically translate into the technical knowledge needed to assess a property, verify its documentation or understand its investment potential. These decisions require proper checks, market understanding and accountability. I’m a physiotherapist, a strategy consultant, a healthcare entrepreneur, and I recently graduated from the University of Oxford with a distinction in Health Service Improvement and Evaluation. I have probably said that last part a hundred times since getting my results, and honestly, I don’t think I’m tired of saying it yet. Haha! One thing about me is that I like to be involved. I am sometimes curious about things that have absolutely nothing to do with what I’m supposed to be doing, and I genuinely enjoy working with people. I like organising things, bringing people together, and seeing an idea move forward to get accomplished. So I have known that going to Oxford was never going to be just about getting a master’s degree. Let me explain how I ended up there. I studied Physiotherapy at the University of Ibadan, where I graduated with First-Class Honours. During my undergraduate years, I was involved in quite a lot outside academics: student leadership, journalism, research, community health programmes and advocacy. My involvement in community health exposed me to how differently people experience healthcare depending on where they live, what they can afford and what information they have access to. I loved being a physiotherapist, and that allowed me to interrogate questions that went beyond individual patient care. Why do some people receive good healthcare while others struggle to access even basic services? How do we make healthcare more affordable? What role can technology play? And why do some seemingly good healthcare programmes struggle to produce lasting change? Eventually, I realised I wanted to study and work in a field that constantly seeks to improve health systems. I researched different programmes across the US and UK, hoping to study at institutions that have international audiences where I could build a diverse perspective in health. I came across the MSc in Health Service Improvement and Evaluation at the University of Oxford’s Nuffield Department of Medicine. It aligned with many of my interests, so I applied. I also needed a scholarship because, quite frankly, I couldn’t afford Oxford. It was a humbling and affirming process. I was awarded scholarships such as the Chevening Scholarship and two Oxford-based scholarships. I still feel fortunate to have received and chosen the Mastercard Foundation-Africa Oxford Initiative Scholarship, which fully funded my studies. I am deeply grateful for that opportunity. Now, I think it’s important to say that I was very excited about the academic programme. I wanted to understand healthcare systems better, learn new research methods and become more effective at designing and evaluating healthcare services. entertainment.title: Elizabeth Agboola: Your Next Flight From Nigeria Could Be Two Holidays in One. Here’s How
entertainment.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. For visa purposes, Nigerians do not qualify, but with a valid Turkish visa you would be able to qualify for some of the perks. Qualifying travellers with connections of at least 20 hours and up to seven days may receive complimentary hotel accommodation. Under the standard programme, eligible Economy Class passengers can receive one night in a four-star hotel, while Business Class passengers may receive two nights in a five-star or boutique hotel. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. Read the full recipe for Rice and Peas with Oxtail . Rice and peas with oxtail, from Episode 1 Soliat Bada and Michael Famoroti in Episode 1 Episode 2 moves to the Gulf for lamb kabsa, Saudi Arabia’s national dish, fragrant with dried lime and seven spice. Soliat is joined by Bella Adeleke , CEO of Asali Africa and founder of the fashion label Garbe, for a conversation about redefining success. Read the full recipe for Lamb Kabsa . Lamb kabsa, from Episode 2 Still to come are Nigerian fried rice with fried turkey and dodo, cooked with Toyin Jolapamo and Nneoma Mere; jambalaya with Goldie Iyamu and Vanessa Iloenyosi ; and a season finale with Edwin Okolo and Temi Omolehinwa. For more on Asali Africa and the products and ideas it develops, visit asali.africa . Episodes 1 and 2 are out now on YouTube. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. Market scale does not, on its own, define technology leadership. What it does provide is evidence that a manufacturer has become an important participant in how the category develops. entertainment.title: A Safari, a Beach & Easy Entry? 5 African Spots for Your Christmas Holiday
entertainment.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. Nigerian citizens enjoy visa-free entry for short stays of up to 60 days without needing a paid eTA, leaving more room in your budget for safaris and coastal stays. Rwanda Not everyone wants their year-end holiday to feel like a non-stop sprint, and Rwanda is built for travellers who prefer scenery, clean air, and an unhurried pace. Days in Kigali easily revolve around specialty coffee shops, contemporary art at Inema Arts Center, and a sobering, essential visit to the Kigali Genocide Memorial before you head out into the countryside. From the capital, you can track chimpanzees and walk above the trees in Nyungwe Forest, go on wildlife drives in Akagera National Park, or spend quiet afternoons along the shores of Lake Kivu. With 30-day visa-free entry for Nigerian passport holders, getting there is straightforward from start to finish. Mauritius Sometimes a proper Christmas break calls for leaving mainland schedules behind altogether for turquoise lagoons, catamaran cruises, and mountain trails. In Mauritius, you can base yourself around Grand Baie in the north for boat trips to Île aux Cerfs and lively beachside dinners, or head south-west toward Le Morne Brabant for coastal hikes and water sports. entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. entertainment.title: How La Roche-Posay Brought Skin Science to Over 500 Guests in Its First Living Lab Experience
entertainment.description: La Roche-Posay concluded its first Living Lab experience in Nigeria, welcoming Nigerian stakeholders to its opening party and three-day programme, held from 4 to 6 November 2026 at Oasis by The Five Palm, Victoria Island, Lagos. Inspired by the original Living Lab concept in Paris, the experience brought the science, research and expertise behind skincare closer to Nigerian consumers and healthcare professionals. It marked the brand’s first Living Lab in the country, creating a platform for more accessible conversations around skin health, dermatological innovation and everyday skincare. The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. Each day featured three expert-led sessions exploring the role of dermatology and scientific research in advancing skin health, the wider impact of skin conditions on everyday life, and the importance of understanding product safety, tolerance and efficacy. The sessions brought together healthcare professionals and representatives from across Nigeria’s dermatological beauty and skincare community, encouraging knowledge-sharing and stronger connections between science, expertise and consumer education. Visitors explored five dedicated Innovation Corners showcasing La Roche-Posay’s Effaclar, Mela B3, Anthelios, Cicaplast and Lipikar ranges. Each space introduced visitors to specific skin concerns and the science behind the brand’s product formulations. Through interactive demonstrations and guided product experiences, guests gained a better understanding of different skin concerns and the role of targeted skincare in addressing them. At the Anthelios corner, visitors used a UV camera to see the effects of ultraviolet exposure and better understand the importance of sun protection. The Effaclar and Mela B3 spaces explored concerns including blemishes and hyperpigmentation, while the Cicaplast and Lipikar corners introduced visitors to approaches to caring for sensitive, damaged and dry skin. Beyond the Innovation Corners, visitors explored the Blue House, which presented La Roche-Posay’s history and commitment to dermatological innovation, and the Scars of Life Cinema. The cinema screened a 25-minute film exploring the physical and psychological realities of living with scars and scarring, including their impact on self-image and everyday life. The film also highlighted how Lipikar supports the care of skin affected by scarring, bringing attention to the importance of addressing both the visible and less visible experiences associated with skin conditions. The programme also created opportunities for visitors to engage with skincare experts and dermatologists through one-on-one consultations, ask questions about their individual skin concerns and receive guidance on building appropriate skincare routines. entertainment.description: One of the best aspects of art is its ability to imitate current events or imagine possibilities. Movies, as a powerful art form, present a sequence of events that allows viewers to see reflections of themselves or envision who they could become. At its core, art exists to entertain, inform and critique society. Through films, music and visual expressions, we are continually reminded of our shared humanity—our joys, flaws and contradictions. One subject that art, particularly film, has explored is masculinity. However, this theme is often addressed subtly and can be easy to overlook, as the movies that dominate global box offices frequently focus on spectacle: fantasy, romance, adventure or others. Conversations about men, their inner lives, vulnerabilities and social roles are often not in the top circle. Nonetheless, some films have attempted to explore what it means to be a man in today’s world. They invite audiences to contemplate important questions such as: What is the role of men in society? Through his struggles with homelessness, rejection, and exhaustion, the film redefines masculinity, depicting it as the courage to remain tender even when life tests your strength in every way. Fatherhood Kevin Hart ’s film Fatherhood delves into themes of grief and single parenthood, balancing humour with heartfelt moments. sports.description: New York Giants cornerback Deonte Banks (2) runs with the ball after an interception during a week 11 NFL football game between New York Giants and Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The New York Giants face a tight window to lock up cornerback Deonte Banks before his contract expires. On Tuesday, Jordan Raanan of ESPN identified Banks as the leading candidate for a contract extension. With 14 pass breakups, the 2023 first-round pick shares the league lead. He enters the final season of his rookie deal, which totals $13.59 million over four years. The team declined his fifth-year option back in May, a move that could cost them dearly now. Banks has turned his career around after being written off by the previous coaching staff. He took the starting job from Paulson Adebo in training camp before the 2026 season. Adebo signed a massive $54 million deal last year, only to lose his spot to a player he was meant to mentor. Alex Wilson from Empire State Media posted on his official X account, “If the depth chart is legit, my god … Paulson Adebo, how did you lose a starting job to Deonte Banks!!!” Setting the Market Price The Denver Broncos recently set a new bar for cornerbacks in their draft class. They signed Riley Moss to a four-year, $67 million extension. That breaks down to $16.75 million per year. The Athletic’s Dan Duggan noted, “Greg Newsome got $15.25M. Data points to keep in mind for Deonte Banks’ negotiations.” Newsome, another Giants cornerback, signed a three-year, $46 million deal earlier this month. The Giants should aim for that range to keep their secondary intact without overpaying. The Athletic’s Dan Duggan wrote, “Looks wise for Greg Newsome to lock in his extension eight games into the season.” He added that missing time with a “serious” high-ankle sprain could hurt a player’s market value. Banks has no such injury concerns and is playing at an elite level right now. Waiting until he hits the open market could push his value well past $20 million per year. sports.title: A year after KKR release, Mustafizur Rahman missing from IPL auction list as 11 Bangladesh players register
sports.description: Mustafizur Rahman is not among the 11 Bangladesh players who have registered for the IPL 2027 auction, which will be held in Goa on December 16. The left-arm pacer was released by Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) on the BCCI's instructions last year, a decision that eventually led to Bangladesh withdrawing from the T20 World Cup in India. BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia did not specify the reason behind Mustafizur's release at the time, saying only that it was due to "recent developments". The 11 Bangladesh players who have entered the auction are Hasan Mahmud, Parvez Hossain Emon, Ripon Mondol, Rishad Hossain, Saif Hassan, Shak Mahedi Hasan, Shamim Hossain, Shoriful Islam, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Towhid Hridoy and Md Rubel. Stokes enters IPL auction Former England captain Ben Stokes and Australian batter Cameron Bancroft are among the prominent overseas players who have registered for the auction. sports.title: Ben Johnson Keeps D’Andre Swift In Bears Run Game Despite Fumble
sports.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images D’Andre Swift will not lose his spot as the lead back for the Chicago Bears after a costly mistake against the New Orleans Saints. Head coach Ben Johnson made his stance clear on Tuesday. The coach rejected the idea that Swift must work to earn back any trust. He said the running back simply needs to secure the football to keep the offense moving forward. Swift lost his third fumble of the season during the fourth quarter. New Orleans recovered the ball at their own 46-yard line. The 27-year-old runner did not return to the game after that turnover. It marks the second time this year Swift was pulled from a lineup for a fumble. Despite these errors, the coach insists the team will keep relying on its rushing attack. The Trust Factor When asked if Swift needs to regain confidence from the coaching staff, Johnson shut down the notion immediately. “No, he just needs to hold on to the ball and we’ll be fine,” Johnson said, according to ESPN . This comment came after the Bears secured a 21-13 win over the Saints on Sunday. The victory improved the team’s record, and the coaching staff continues to focus on ball security. Swift has fumbled three times through the first ten games. This is the most he has lost since the 2023 season. Michal Dwojak noted that Swift still holds the head coach’s trust according to RotoBaller. In that game, the veteran back recorded his first touchdown catch of the year. He led the backfield with 15 touches, including two catches for eight yards and a score. Running Game Efficiency The Bears offense relies heavily on moving the chains on the ground. The team ranks third in the league with 142.4 rushing yards per game. However, Johnson was not happy with the efficiency numbers in the recent win. The team rushed for 146 yards against New Orleans, their third-highest total of the year. Yet the average yards per carry fell short of the goal. “We weren’t as consistent running the ball as we had wanted to be coming off the bye, that was a point of emphasis for us,” Johnson said postgame. Swift ran 13 times for 51 yards, averaging 3.9 yards per carry. Johnson pointed out that the runners were under four yards a carry. “When I looked at our runners, they were under four yards a carry. That efficiency stat that we talked about, we weren’t hitting that,” Johnson said. Upcoming Matchup Other backs saw action in the game as well. In his first game back after toe and thumb injuries, Kyle Monangai rushed eight times for 18 yards. Monangai played 23 offensive snaps compared to Swift’s 28. Salvon Ahmed added six carries to the mix. The coaching staff will look to balance the workload while fixing the ball security issues before the next game. “We’re going to continue to stress that running game,” Johnson said Tuesday. The Bears must prepare for a tough road test against a division rival. The team will face the Detroit Lions on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 1 p.m. ET at Ford Field.

sports.title: FC Barcelona Vs Sabah Line Up: Solutions And Rotations Without Lamine
sports.description: FC Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick will make several rotations for Wednesday's Champions League trip to Baku. We already knew that Lamine Yamal wouldn’t travel to Baku, after the club released a statement explaining that the youngster is suffering from ankle discomfort. sports.title: Rinderknech denies refusing doping test
sports.description: Arthur Rinderknech is yet to win an ATP title and reached a highest world ranking of 24th in May [Getty Images] French tennis player Arthur Rinderknech says he expects to be exonerated over allegations he refused a doping test. L'Equipe reported on Wednesday that the current world number 57 is under investigation by the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA). It relates to a "surprise" test in June, with French newspaper L'Equipe claiming there was a "possible misunderstanding with the sample collector". Former Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova is currently serving a four-year ban for refusing to take an out-of-competition doping test in December 2025, and has appealed against the decision. Rinderknech issued a statement on Instagram in response to L'Equipe's report, saying: "I have already advised the ITIA that I deny the allegation and I have already requested that the matter be heard and determined by an independent tribunal, as is my right." The 31-year-old, who beat current world number one Alexander Zverev in the first round at Wimbledon last year, believes he will then be "exonerated of the test refusal allegation". "I have never taken any banned substance and I am proud of my accomplishments in professional tennis, all of which have been achieved through hard work and with integrity always," he added. sports.title: Jude Bellingham explains why he’s no match for Zinedine Zidane after shining for Real Madrid
sports.description: Jude Bellingham has played down comparisons to Real Madrid legend Zinedine Zidane after inspiring victory in the Champions League with a sensational goal against PSV. The England international juggled the ball in the air before swiping a volley into the back of the net, leaving fans and teammates in awe, including Bernardo Silva: “It was one of those moments when you just go, ‘Wow!’” The win maintains Madrid’s perfect Champions League record, elevating them to serious contenders to dethrone two-time defending champions Paris Saint-Germain, while rising up The Independent’s power rankings . And after Mourinho described Bellingham as “without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world,” comparisons continue with one of Madrid’s all-time greatest players: Zidane. But Bellingham was quick to distance himself from the conversation, instead placing the France manager in an entirely different category. "I was a bit surprised, honestly. I knew that I could control the ball well and get it into my grasp. "It popped up nicely and I thought I'm just going to hit it. So yeah, it was a nice goal and important for the team, being the second goal, and gave us control. Bellingham scored a stunning volley in the second half (Getty) "I think Zidane is much better than me. He's much more elegant and he's my idol.” Mourinho was left stunned by his player’s latest impact, pinpointing just what makes him so good. "He is an amazing player that has everything," the Portuguese manager said. "He has physicality, he understands the game, he has absolutely everything. Today, he has changed how the game was evolving." “Obviously Jude is a different type of player and he gave us what we didn't have in the first half,” Mourinho said. “He changed the game, scored an incredible goal.”

sports.title: As Farmageddon's streak ends, Kansas State and Iowa State hope it's not for long
sports.description: MANHATTAN — When Skylar Thompson first arrived at Kansas State , he knew about the rivalry against Kansas, but when he sat at a team dinner and heard the seniors talk about the importance of beating Iowa State , he learned there was a second rivalry that was almost as important . Winning that game suddenly didn't matter as much for personal pride . Instead, it became about winning for the fanbase, the seniors and the university. Thompson was behind center as a redshirt freshman in 2017 when the Wildcats were down by five against the Cyclones with eight seconds left from the one-yard line. Thompson looked to his left, and no one was open as he scrambled that way. With a defender in his face, he changed direction to the other side of the field. He ran, seemingly forever, until he found Isaiah Zuber in the back of the endzone as time expired . Wildcats win. "That was probably one of my most fond memories at K-State," Thompson said. Nicknamed "Farmageddon" for the agricultural roots of being two land-grant universities, Kansas State and Iowa State have played the longest uninterrupted continuous series in college football, having played each season since 1917. The 110th-straight game between the two will be played on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 1 p.m. CT at Jack Trice Stadium in Ames, Iowa. Saturday will also mark the end of the uninterrupted series, as the two are not scheduled to play next season. "We definitely wanted to play it," K-State athletic director Gene Taylor said. "But we knew that everybody was gonna get to play a second rival. We kind of had to take our lumps and agree to the way the scheduling matrix turned out." When the Big 12 added Arizona, Arizona State , Colorado and Utah to expand the league to 16 teams, the reconfigured scheduling matrix chose four "protected" rivalries that wouldn't go away, and Kansas State-Kansas was one of them. That put Farmageddon on the chopping block. When the matrix was released ahead of the 2024 season, it was known the Wildcats' annual game against the Cyclones would end in 2027. A new matrix will need to be developed ahead of the 2028 season, which could see the return of the game sooner rather than later. That's something Taylor expects to happen. With all of the changes in the sport, especially with the 24-team College Football Playoff that will begin in 2027, scheduling will be at the forefront. "I think it may not be as long of a hiatus as we think it was; in essence, there was gonna be a period of 2-3 years where we weren't going to play," Taylor said. "We may have to rethink the entire scheduling model here coming up. I think our fanbase wanted to keep it; there's no question. I think there's a lot of reasons to keep it in the future." Farmageddon predated the Big 8, let alone the Big 12, beginning in 1917 when K-State and Iowa State were both members of a previous iteration of the Missouri Valley Conference. More: Youngman family runs together, bonds together The Colts finished the 2026 season with a 15-4-2 overall record, capturing their seventh consecutive district championship and reaching the Division 4 regional championship game for the first time since 2020. Ohio State and Michigan will play on Nov. 28 in the 129th year of the rivalry. Last year, Ohio State beat Michigan 27-9 and snapped a four-game losing streak to the Wolverines dating back to a 42-27 loss to Michigan in 2021. This year's rivalry game will have a different feel . Ohio State and Michigan combine for nine losses this season, with the 7-4 Buckeyes and 6-5 Wolverines essentially out of the hunt for a College Football Playoff spot. And it means everything to us." The two schools' storied rivalry includes fights , historic upsets and longstanding traditions leading up to The Game, including Ohio State fans crossing out the letter 'M' in Columbus. When did the Ohio State-Michigan rivalry begin? Some historians trace the rivalry to the " Toledo War ," a land dispute between Ohio and Michigan when Michigan was applying for statehood in the 19th century. Ohio and the Michigan territory disputed over the rights to the Toledo strip, a 450-square-mile area in the northwest region of Ohio's border and Michigan's established territory. Michigan's repeated applications for statehood were denied because it refused to give up the Toledo strip. After decades, the dispute ended in 1836 when a compromise was formed. Ohio claimed Toledo as well as the Maumee River and Maumee Bay. In exchange, the Michigan territory was given a region called the Upper Peninsula. Michigan became an official state in 1837. At the time, Michigan residents believed they got the short end of the deal; the Michigan Territory was also believed to have been planning the University of Michigan in Toledo rather than Ann Arbor. When was the first Ohio State-Michigan football game? Ohio State and Michigan's first recorded football game came 128 years ago on Oct. 16, 1897. Ball State (3-8, 2-5 MAC) will host Central Michigan (5-6, 3-4 MAC) in the regular season finale for both teams on Saturday, Nov. 28. The Cardinals are looking to bounce back from a three-game losing streak during their primetime midweek MACtion slate, while the Chippewas will look to rebound from a loss to Buffalo. sports.title: WSL makes agreement with clubs to avoid gambling sponsors
sports.description: WSL Football, the organisation responsible for operating the top two tiers of women’s football in the UK, has reached an agreement in principle for its clubs not to make sponsorship deals with betting companies. Instead, the organisation has agreed to pursue sponsorship deals with brands from different industries, reports The Athletic . The outlet states that six additional sponsorship opportunities were made available ahead of the 2024/25 season, and these were filled by Apple, Airbnb, British Gas, Mercedes, Tesco and WTW. While the agreement applies to WSL Football’s own commercial partnerships, it does not stop individual WSL or WSL2 clubs from signing sponsorship deals with gambling companies. Rather, it sets a different direction for WSL Football’s league-level partnerships, giving the leagues the chance to shape their own commercial future. The organisation wants to continue aiding the growth of the women’s domestic game, while combating issues such as player welfare, gambling-related online abuse and fluctuating attendances. The changes also come at a time when English football is starting to take a wider look at gambling and related sponsorships. At the start of this season, the Premier League’s voluntary ban on betting sponsors appearing on the front of match-day shirts came into effect, while the Premier League, EFL, FA and WSL also introduced a Code of Conduct for gambling-related sponsorship agreements in 2024. Nevertheless, betting companies still feature prominently among sponsors at clubs throughout the top divisions in the men’s game, with Betway signing a deal with Manchester United and clubs such as Leeds and Nottingham Forest also agreeing new deals over the summer.
